overview: Laos is the only landlocked country in South-East Asia. Its capital and largest city is Vientiane. Laos became independent from France in 1953 and has been a communist state since 1975. Most people are Buddhist, and the old royal city of Luang Prabang is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

geography.text: Laos is mostly mountainous and covered in forest. The Mekong river runs through much of the country and forms a long stretch of the border with Thailand. In the far south it spreads out among the 'Four Thousand Islands' and plunges over the Khone Falls. The Plain of Jars in the north is scattered with large ancient stone jars.

history.text: The kingdom of Lan Xang, the 'land of a million elephants', was founded in 1353. Laos later came under Siamese control and then became part of French Indochina. It became independent in 1953. During the Vietnam War, the United States dropped more bombs on Laos than it dropped on Germany and Japan together in the Second World War, and the communist Pathet Lao took power in 1975.

events.title: Lan Xang
events.text: Fa Ngum founds the kingdom of Lan Xang.

events.title: French rule
events.text: Laos becomes part of French Indochina.

events.title: Secret bombing
events.text: A US bombing campaign begins that lasts nine years.

government.text: Laos is a one-party communist state ruled by the Lao People's Revolutionary Party since 1975. The National Assembly elects the President, who is head of state, and the Prime Minister leads the government.

economy.text: Most Laotians work in farming, growing rice. Laos sells hydropower to its neighbours and has been called 'the battery of South-East Asia'. A railway to China opened in 2021, but heavy borrowing has left the country with large debts.

culture.text: Laos is a Buddhist country, and early each morning in Luang Prabang, saffron-robed monks walk the streets collecting alms. Sticky rice is eaten with almost every meal. Unexploded bombs from the Vietnam War still lie in the countryside.

items.title: Luang Prabang
items.text: A royal city of temples listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Plain of Jars
items.text: Thousands of mysterious stone jars more than 2,000 years old.

items.title: Sticky rice
items.text: Eaten with the hands at almost every meal.

sport.text: Football and sepak takraw, a kind of volleyball played with the feet, are popular. Laos sends small teams to the Olympics.

items.title: Sepak takraw
items.text: A rattan ball kicked over a net.
